questions.q: Which command confirms Git is installed?
questions.explain: git --version prints the installed version.

questions.q: Why use an SSH key with GitHub?
options: It authenticates you without typing a password
questions.explain: SSH keys prove who you are on every push and pull.

questions.q: What does 2FA protect against?
options: Someone logging in with a stolen password
questions.explain: A second factor stops a leaked password from being enough.

questions.q: What does LTS mean for Node.js?
questions.explain: LTS releases get fixes for a long time, so teams standardise on them.

questions.q: Where should secrets like API tokens live?
options: In an environment file that is never committed
questions.explain: Keep secrets in env files listed in .gitignore, or in a secrets manager.

questions.q: Which command shows files you changed but have not committed?
questions.explain: git status shows the working folder and staging area.

questions.q: What does 'git add' do?
options: Moves changes into the staging area
questions.explain: Staging chooses what goes into the next commit.

questions.q: Which push option is the safe way to overwrite a remote branch you own?
questions.explain: --force-with-lease refuses if someone else pushed in the meantime.

questions.q: You committed with a typo in the message and have not pushed. What fixes it?
questions.explain: --amend rewrites the last commit, which is fine before pushing.

questions.q: What causes a merge conflict?
options: Two branches changed the same lines differently
A branch has too many commits
questions.explain: Git cannot pick between two different edits to the same lines, so it asks you.

questions.q: What is a pull request?
options: A request to download a repo
A proposal to merge one branch into another, with review
questions.explain: PRs let the team review a change before it merges.

questions.q: What makes a PR easy to review?
options: A small, focused change with a clear description
questions.explain: Small and focused PRs get faster, better reviews.

questions.q: A reviewer asks for a change. What do you do?
options: Push a new commit that addresses it and reply
questions.explain: Address the comment, push, and reply so the reviewer knows.

questions.q: What does 'Closes #12' in a PR description do?
options: Closes issue 12 when the PR merges
questions.explain: GitHub links the PR to the issue and closes it on merge.

questions.q: Why protect the main branch?
options: So changes only land through reviewed, passing PRs
questions.explain: Branch protection enforces review and green checks before merge.

questions.q: What does CI stand for?
questions.explain: CI builds and tests every change automatically.

questions.q: Where do GitHub Actions workflows live?
questions.explain: Each YAML file in .github/workflows/ is a workflow.

questions.q: CI fails on your PR. What first?
questions.explain: The log tells you which step failed and why.

questions.q: What is a unit test?
options: A test of one small piece of code in isolation
questions.explain: Unit tests check one function or module quickly.

questions.q: Why run tests locally before pushing?
options: Faster feedback and fewer red PRs
questions.explain: Catching failures early saves everyone time.

questions.q: What belongs in a stand-up update?
questions.explain: Keep it short: what you did, what you will do, what blocks you.

questions.q: You are stuck for over an hour. What should you do?
options: Ask in the team chat with what you tried
questions.explain: Asking early with context is a strength, not a weakness.

questions.q: What is a good-first-issue?
options: A small, well-scoped task for newcomers
A feature request from a customer
questions.explain: They are picked so a newcomer can ship quickly.

questions.q: What is a retro for?
options: Learning what to keep and what to change
questions.explain: Retros turn experience into improvements.

questions.q: When is a task 'done'?
options: When it is merged, tested and meets the acceptance criteria
When you start the next task
questions.explain: Done means it works, is reviewed and is merged.
